items.title: 24.6.1 Acidic and Basic Properties of Amino Acids

source_refs.note: Topic 24.6.1 (PDF 130); the equilibria are shown in the figure of topic 24.6.

blocks.text: Amino acids are amphoteric, but they are less acidic than most carboxylic acids and less basic than most amines. The acidic part of the amino acid molecule is the -NH3+ group, not -COOH, and the basic part is the -COO- group, not -NH2. RNH3+ is a weaker acid than RCOOH:

In aqueous solution an equilibrium exists between the dipolar ion and the cationic and anionic forms of an amino acid. The cationic form, H3N+-CH(R)-COOH, is predominant at low pH; the dipolar ion at the isoelectric pH; and the anionic form, H2N-CH(R)-COO-, at high pH.

blocks.title: Isoelectric point (pI)
blocks.text: The isoelectric point is the pH at which the concentration of the zwitterion is at its maximum and the amino acid has no overall charge. Each amino acid has its own pI.

blocks.prompt: In which form is an amino acid present in a strongly acidic solution?
blocks.explanation: The cationic form, H3N+-CH(R)-COOH: the carboxylate group has taken a proton.

items: Acidic part -NH3+ (pKa about 10); basic part -COO- (pKb about 12).
Low pH: cation; pI: zwitterion; high pH: anion.
